x-e-e6-03.title: Book club dey succeed? Change your judgment as evidence increase
x-e-e6-03.goal: As data dey come one part at a time, change your judgment about di claim 'di book club dey succeed', then finish for English with two pieces of evidence.
x-e-e6-03.material: New book club start for our school. Teacher talk say, "Di club dey succeed." Dem go give you evidence one part at a time, and you go think whether di statement correct.
x-e-e6-03.thinking.0: No decide from only one piece of evidence
x-e-e6-03.thinking.1: Change your judgment when new information show
x-e-e6-03.thinking.2: Write one claim by joining different pieces of evidence
x-e-e6-03.prereq.1: Easy expressions like sign up, only, come
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.prompt: Check di data one part at a time, and each time choose wetin you think about di statement 'The club is a success'.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.hint.0: Separate wetin di data wey you get now confirm from wetin you still no know.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether new data dey point same direction as earlier data or opposite direction.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.info: For March, 12 students sign up for di club.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: From only this data, wetin you think about 'Di club dey succeed'?
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.after: Number of people wey sign up show how e start. You need see how dem actually take part afterward.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This one reach conclusion only from number wey sign up. We still no know wetin dem do after signing up.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: E no dey succeed. Clubs no dey popular at all.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This one reach conclusion from general statement wey no dey inside di data.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: We never know yet. Signing up na only di beginning.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This one show di limit of di evidence wey we get now.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.info: Only 4 students come to May meeting.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now data don increase. How you see am now?
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Plenty people sign up but fewer come. Evidence for 'success' don weak, but we still no know why di number drop.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Di first number matter pass, so e dey succeed.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This one make di new data fit di first judgment.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This one lower di judgment by combining both pieces of data.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: No standard for 'few' dey, but e jump straight to conclusion.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Each of di 4 wey come read 3 books every month. At di same time, 6 students move to sports club wey meet same time.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: Now, wetin be di best conclusion?
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.after: Attendance drop, but students wey come read plenty books, and drop fit happen because time overlap. We need more information before we conclude.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: E drop because book club boring.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: 'Boring' na reason wey data no mention.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Students wey come read well, and drop fit happen because time overlap. We need ask more.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This separate facts for data from wetin we still no know.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Na only 4 wey come work hard, so club successful.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This decide for everybody from result of only some students.
x-e-e6-03.s.s1.reflect: At first e look like 'success', but your judgment change every time new evidence come. You must fit change judgment as evidence add up.
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.prompt: Write 1 or 2 English sentences. Say whether you think book club successful and include 2 evidence from data above.
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.hint.0: First state your thought in one sentence. (I think / I am not sure ...)
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.hint.1: Use but to connect second evidence (one of attendance, books, sports club).
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.placeholder: Example: I am not sure ... because ...
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Each evidence match correct stage of data?
x-e-e6-03.s.s2.modelNote.1: Answer wey give both part of success and its limits.

x-e-e6-04.title: Make tables to find cases where claim true
x-e-e6-04.goal: Make several vote tables yourself where English claim 'e get most votes but no reach half the class' true.
x-e-e6-04.material: 20 students in one class each vote one time for after-snack activity: soccer, art or music. Votes call s (soccer), a (art), and m (music).
x-e-e6-04.thinking.1: Make examples wey meet several conditions at once
x-e-e6-04.prereq.1: Meaning of most, fewer than, half
x-e-e6-04.s.s1.prompt: Result na soccer 8 votes, art 6, music 6. Which sentence describe am most correctly?
x-e-e6-04.s.s1.hint.0: Add 8, 6 and 6; find half of 20 students and compare.
x-e-e6-04.s.s1.r.a: Check whether both conditions confirmed with numbers.
x-e-e6-04.s.s1.r.c: Check again whether 8 bigger or smaller than 10.
x-e-e6-04.s.s1.explain: 8 votes pass art (6) and music (6), so e get most votes; e below 10, half of 20, so e no reach half. Therefore a correct.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different vote tables with 20 students total where same claim ('soccer get most votes but not half') true.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.hint.0: Soccer must get most, so start by choosing a number bigger than art and music.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.hint.1: Set soccer votes to one value, subtract am from 20, then divide rest between art and music. If soccer number too small, total no go reach 20.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Votes na whole numbers 0 or bigger.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Write votes as whole numbers 0 or bigger.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.fail.c3: Soccer votes no pass art or music.
x-e-e6-04.s.s2.explain: For soccer get most, both art and music must each be smaller than s, and together dem add to 20−s. If s=7, then a+m=13, so dem no fit both be 6 or less; e fail. If s=10 or more, na half at least. So s fit only be 8 or 9.

x-e-e6-09.title: Rewrite meeting notice so new friend Emma fit read am

x-e-e6-09.material:
Jun write this for class group chat.
"BTW, we go meet for di usual place after school. Bring di stuff!"

Emma, wey just transfer enter this class today, dey inside di chat too. Emma no know di school well.

Abeg note: di usual place na bench under big tree beside playground, and di stuff na ball and water bottles.
x-e-e6-09.thinking.0: Separate wetin reader already know from wetin reader no know
x-e-e6-09.thinking.2: Check whether message fit understand by itself
x-e-e6-09.prereq.0: Easy words like place, bring, after school
x-e-e6-09.prereq.1: gonna na how people dey pronounce going to
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose every part wey go confuse Emma because she no go know wetin e mean when she read am.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.hint.0: Since Emma no know di school well, find which words only people wey don spend time together fit know.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.hint.1: Ask yourself whether person fit understand each expression without explanation.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.r.a: Some people fit no know abbreviations, but if you work out di meaning, e fit no affect understanding much.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.r.b: Na only friends wey dey together know where 'di place wey we always dey go' be.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.r.c: Na general expression wey anybody fit understand.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.r.d: Dem no explain wetin person suppose bring.
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.explain: b and d na words wey you fit know only if dem don discuss am before, so Emma no know where to meet or wetin to bring. 'BTW' okay to leave without explanation because not knowing am no cause big problem to understand di meaning, so we accept both (a fit work too).
x-e-e6-09.s.s1.acc.0: BTW (by the way) na abbreviation wey person wey dey see am first time fit no know too, so you fit fix am also.
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite di message with two or three English sentences so Emma fit understand am too. Include exactly where to meet and wetin to bring.
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.hint.0: Replace 'the usual place' and 'the stuff' with di explanation dem give you.
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.hint.1: Adding greeting for Emma go make am warmer.
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Even if Emma no sabi di school, she fit find di place?
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.selfAssess.1: She fit know wetin she suppose bring?
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Di tone make Emma feel welcome?
x-e-e6-09.s.s2.modelNote.1: Answer wey be like announcement to everybody.

x-e-e6-10.title: Same message about coming late: how you go fix am when reader change?
x-e-e6-10.goal: As dem dey add information about reader one by one, decide how to fix di text message, and rewrite am for English to suit new reader.
x-e-e6-10.material: Jisu wan write text: "Hi! I'll be late. The meeting went long." Every time di person wey go read di text change, judge whether e fit am.
x-e-e6-10.thinking.0: Know say wetin person need change when information about reader change
x-e-e6-10.thinking.2: Write message wey person fit understand by itself
x-e-e6-10.prereq.0: Easy words like late, meeting, arrive
x-e-e6-10.prereq.1: Phrase to introduce yourself with this is ~
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.prompt: Look at information about reader one by one, and each time choose wetin go good to do with this text.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.hint.0: First write down wetin reader already know (me, meeting, schedule).
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.hint.1: Find wetin that person no know for di text.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.info: Di person wey go receive am na Jisu mama. Mama know say Jisu get school book club meeting today.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin go good to do with di text?
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.after: Mama know about di meeting and know who dey write, so this short text enough.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Start with your name and class number so dem go know who dey write.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Mama already know say na text from Jisu.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Start with "Dear Mom," and add long, polite apology.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Think whether reader na person wey close to you.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E enough to send am as e be.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This consider wetin reader already know.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.info: Now person wey go receive am don change to Mr. Brown, neighbor wey Jisu dey meet for first time. Mr. Brown no know Jisu, and dem agree to meet today.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.after: Mr. Brown no know who Jisu be, wetin kind of meeting e be, or when Jisu go arrive. These three things need to dey inside di text.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This no consider say reader don change.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Put who I be, which meeting e be, and when I go arrive.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This try fill wetin reader no know.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Use more abbreviations make e look friendly.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Other words wey reader no know fit dey.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.2.info: Mr. Brown na adult and e no reach long wey e come Korea.

x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.2.after: For adult wey you dey meet for first time, e good to greet am, say who you be, and use words wey person wey just come Korea recently fit understand.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This consider say reader na adult and newcomer.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Adult wey just come Korea recently fit no know abbreviations and emoticons.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Mr. Brown no know Jisu, and "It's me" no tell am who e be.
x-e-e6-10.s.s1.reflect: Even with same news, di information wey dem need and di tone change when reader change. You must ask again every time wetin reader no know.
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.prompt: Write two or three English sentences as text to send Mr. Brown. Include greeting, who you be, which meeting, and how late you go be.
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.hint.0: Think about wetin Mr. Brown no know about Jisu, then decide wetin to write for beginning of di text.
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.hint.1: For one sentence, write which meeting e be and how late (or wetin time) you go arrive, including number.
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Hello, Mr. Brown. This is ...
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Mr. Brown fit tell who Jisu be?
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: E clear which meeting e be and when Jisu go arrive?
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Di tone suit writing to adult?
x-e-e6-10.s.s2.modelNote.1: Answer wey clearly include apology and how late you go be.

x-e-e6-06.title: Joy go really late? Choose wetin to check and wetin to ask
x-e-e6-06.goal: Sort wetin you need know before claim 'bus slow, so I go late' fit hold, then turn am to English questions.
x-e-e6-06.material: Joy say, 'My bus dey slow, so tomorrow I go reach school late.'
x-e-e6-06.thinking.0: Separate information needed for conclusion from irrelevant information
x-e-e6-06.prereq.1: Question forms like What time ~? / Will you ~?
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.prompt: Wetin information you need to check whether Joy statement right? Choose every one wey fit.
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.hint.0: Read every option and ask, 'If I know this, my judgment about whether Joy late go change?'
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.hint.1: Split Joy words into 2 parts, 'reason → conclusion', and find wetin must be true for conclusion to hold.
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.r.a: Even if you know bus company or driver name, you no know when Joy reach school. Think if e connect to conclusion.
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.r.b: Think why you need definition of late and arrival time.
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.r.c: Number of seats no connect to arrival time. Think if e affect conclusion.
x-e-e6-06.s.s1.r.d: Think whether claim assume say she go ride that bus tomorrow.

x-e-e6-06.s.s2.prompt: Write one English question to ask Joy about what you want check. (Ask for information you chose in s1.)

x-e-e6-06.s.s2.hint.1: Choose one piece of information you absolutely need to know whether Joy right, then ask directly in a sentence.
x-e-e6-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: If she answer, you fit decide whether statement right?
x-e-e6-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Your question clear in one sentence?
x-e-e6-06.s.s2.selfAssess.2: E ask for information, not state conclusion?

x-e-e6-01.title: Sort out di reasons to keep class pet
x-e-e6-01.goal: For Jin opinion text, separate di opinion itself, reasons, examples wey act as evidence, and off-topic talk, then judge in English which reason strong pass.
x-e-e6-01.material:
Class 6-3 dey talk about "Should we keep a class pet?" Na Jin text be this.

I think we should get a class pet. A pet can teach us to take care of animals. I like cats very much, and I want to see one every day. Class 6-1 had a fish last year, and students fed it by turns. Also, many students are afraid of dogs.
x-e-e6-01.thinking.0: Separate opinion from reasons wey support am
x-e-e6-01.thinking.1: Separate personal taste from evidence wey person fit check
x-e-e6-01.thinking.2: Compare how strong di reasons be
x-e-e6-01.prereq.0: You fit read opinion expressions like I think ~ / because
x-e-e6-01.prereq.1: Easy words like fish, pet, feed
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose every sentence wey give reason to support Jin opinion 'we should get a class pet'.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.hint.0: For every sentence, ask yourself whether e support di idea say di whole class suppose keep pet.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.hint.1: Separate sentences wey only show speaker feeling, like 'I like ...', from facts wey other people fit check.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.r.a: This sentence talk about benefit to di class. Also compare am with di opinion: na just same thing wey dem repeat?
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.r.b: Think whether speaker personal taste na reason for di whole class.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.r.c: This sentence use something wey really happen as example. Think how e connect with di claim.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.r.d: Decide whether this na reason to keep pet generally, or worry about only some animals.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.r.e: Check whether this sentence na reason or na di claim itself.
x-e-e6-01.s.s1.explain: a na reason wey name one benefit of keeping animal, and c na evidence because e be example wey another class really try. b na only Jin personal taste, no be reason di class need, d dey talk against some animals, and e no be reason, na di claim itself.
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.prompt: Write one or two sentences to Jin for English. Say which of Jin reasons strongest, and explain why (or talk wetin else dem need).
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.hint.0: Choose one strong reason and take one or two words from that sentence use for your answer.
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.hint.1: Use because or so to connect 'why e strong'.
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You talk which sentence for Jin text your chosen reason come from?
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You explain why di reason strong (or wetin else dem need)?
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You judge di reasons for whole class, no be your personal taste? (optional)
x-e-e6-01.s.s2.modelNote.1: Answer wey point out weakness for one reason (e no get example).

x-e-e6-07.title: Write reply to politely refuse friend birthday invitation
